task.question: What maximum distance did the crew of Artemis II reach from Earth on April 6, 2026?
task.evidence: April 6 – The crew of Artemis II breaks the record for the furthest humans have ever been from Earth, reaching a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) as they travel around the far side of the Moon.

Content: ...Artemis II is the second flight of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft. The crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), and Christina Koch (mission specialist), and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist). The mission is a crewed test flight around the Moon and back, with a planned duration of approximately 10 days. The mission is a free-return trajectory around the Moon, similar to Apollo 13. The crew reached a maximum distance of 6,674 miles (10,741 km) from Earth during the initial phase of the mission on April 6, 2026, before the spacecraft performed a translunar injection burn to head toward the Moon.
